mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer and business confidence declines.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a rise in UNRATE above 10%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production indicates reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings and revenues decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 60-day windows following a decline in INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP indicates reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer and business spending decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a decline in GDPC1, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment combined with stagnant employment growth suggests a weakening labor market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a rise in UNRATE and stagnant PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation combined with rising federal funds rate suggests tighter monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following rising CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate in a tightening monetary cycle may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and consumption decreases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a 0.5% increase in FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending suggests increased demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and earnings grow.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 5-day windows following RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.
